outcomes.text: identify themselves as male or female according to Genesis 1:27
describe how they cope with happy or sad feelings
make the right choices guided by the word of God
appreciate his or her gender as guided by the scriptures

skills.name: Identify themselves as male or female as God created them (Genesis 1:27)
skills.mastery: Says that God created people male and female in his own image (Genesis 1:27), names himself or herself as a boy (male) or a girl (female), and says both boys and girls are made by God and equally loved. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: Saying what one likes about oneself comes before seeing oneself as God made one. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
God as the creator of everything, from Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Describe how to cope with happy and sad feelings
skills.mastery: Describes good ways of coping with feelings: when happy, share joy, sing, thank God; when sad, angry or afraid, pray, talk to a parent, teacher or friend, sing, rest, play; and knows that hitting, breaking things or hiding the feeling forever do not help. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.1, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.2, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.3, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.4, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.5), never as a phone question: c) make the right choices guided by the word of God.
question_forms: good or bad way to cope

prerequisites.reason: Knowing oneself as God made one comes before handling one's feelings. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Knowing what one likes about oneself. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God loves boys more than girls (or girls more than boys).

example.question: Whom did God create in his image, according to Genesis 1:27?
example.correct_answer: Both male and female

misconceptions.cause: The child has heard one gender praised more at home or in play.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only boys" beside "Both male and female" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 1:27 slowly: male and female he created them. Both in God's image.
misconceptions.feedback: God created both boys and girls in his image. He loves them equally.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks parents alone decide whether a baby is a boy or a girl.

example.question: Who created people male and female?
example.correct_answer: God

misconceptions.cause: Babies come from parents, so parents seem to decide everything.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Parents choose" beside "God" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Link Genesis 1:27 and Psalm 139:13: God forms each child.
misconceptions.feedback: God created people male and female.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a child is a boy or a girl because of the chores or games he or she does.

example.question: Wanjiru plays football. Is she still a girl?
example.correct_answer: Yes, she is a girl God made

misconceptions.cause: Activities are often split by gender at home.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, football is for boys" beside "Yes, she is a girl God made" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List activities both boys and girls do. Being a boy or girl is how God made you, not what you play.
misconceptions.feedback: A girl who plays football is still a girl. God made her a girl.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks "made in God's image" means people look exactly like God's face.

example.question: What does "made in God's image" teach us?
example.correct_answer: Each person is special to God and can love and do good like him

misconceptions.cause: Image is used at home for a photo.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "We look exactly like God" beside "Each person is special to God and can love and do good like him" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Talk about a child "taking after" a parent in kindness, not only looks.
misconceptions.feedback: Being made in God's image means each person is special to God.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a sad feeling should be hidden and never told to anyone.

example.question: You feel very sad. What can you do?
example.wrong_answer: Keep it inside and tell nobody
example.correct_answer: Pray and talk to a parent or teacher

misconceptions.cause: The child has been told not to cry or complain.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Keep it inside and tell nobody" beside "Pray and talk to a parent or teacher" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Role-play telling a trusted adult. Say: sharing a sad feeling helps.
misconceptions.feedback: When you are sad, pray and tell someone you trust.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks hitting back is the way to stop feeling angry.

example.question: A friend takes your pencil and you feel angry. What should you do?
example.correct_answer: Calm down, talk to him or tell the teacher

misconceptions.cause: Hitting back is common in play and seems fair.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Hit him" beside "Calm down, talk to him or tell the teacher" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Practise calm steps: breathe, count, speak, get help.
misconceptions.feedback: When angry, calm down and talk. Hitting makes things worse.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks being happy means showing off or laughing at others.

example.question: You got the best marks. What is a good way to show you are happy?
example.correct_answer: Thank God and share your joy kindly

misconceptions.cause: Winning games often comes with teasing.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Laugh at those who failed" beside "Thank God and share your joy kindly" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Contrast two pictures: a child laughing at others and a child thanking God and helping.
misconceptions.feedback: When you are happy, thank God and be kind to others.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God does not care about children's small feelings, so prayer is only for big problems.

example.question: Can a child pray to God when sad about a small thing?
example.correct_answer: Yes, God cares about how we feel

misconceptions.cause: God is pictured as caring only about big matters.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, God is busy" beside "Yes, God cares about how we feel" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 1 Peter 5:7 (cast all your anxiety on him) in simple words.
misconceptions.feedback: You can tell God about any feeling. He cares for you.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

learning_experiences: name members of their family,
tell how they relate with family members,
draw and colour the family tree,

Links to other Learning Activity Areas: Environmental Activities: learners draw the family tree to understand family relationships.

outcomes.text: name family members in the nuclear and extended family
draw the family tree to understand family relationships
desire to respect family members for harmonious living

skills.name: Name members of the nuclear and the extended family
skills.mastery: Names members of the nuclear family (father, mother, brothers, sisters) and the extended family (grandparents, uncles, aunts, cousins), says how each is related (my mother's mother is my grandmother; my father's brother is my uncle), and reads a simple family tree. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception. Practical, marked by the teacher with the KICD rubric (CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.1, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.2, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.3, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.4, CRE.G3.RUBRIC.1.5), never as a phone question: b) draw the family tree to understand family relationships.

prerequisites.reason: Naming family members, from Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
The extended family met in Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Puts grandparents in the nuclear family because they live in the same home.

example.question: Is a grandmother part of the nuclear or the extended family?
example.correct_answer: Extended

misconceptions.cause: Many children live with grandparents in one home.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nuclear" beside "Extended" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw the nuclear family in the middle circle (father, mother, children) and the extended family around it. Grandmother may live with you and still be extended.
misconceptions.feedback: Grandparents are part of the extended family, even if they live with you.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a cousin is a brother or sister.

example.question: Your aunt's son is your...?
example.correct_answer: Cousin

misconceptions.cause: Cousins are often called brothers and sisters at home.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Brother" beside "Cousin" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Trace on a family tree: aunt, then her son, a cousin.
misconceptions.feedback: Your aunt's or uncle's child is your cousin.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks an uncle is only the father's brother, not the mother's.

example.question: Is your mother's brother your uncle?
example.correct_answer: Yes

misconceptions.cause: Different words are used in some home languages.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No, uncles are father's brothers" beside "Yes" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show both sides of a family tree with uncles on each.
misconceptions.feedback: Your mother's brother and your father's brother are both your uncles.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a family must have both a father and a mother, so a child with a guardian has no family.

example.question: Achieng lives with her grandmother. Does she have a family?
example.correct_answer: Yes, her grandmother and those who care for her are her family

misconceptions.cause: Pictures in books show one shape of family.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "No" beside "Yes, her grandmother and those who care for her are her family" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show many family pictures. Say: family is the people God gives to love and care for us.
misconceptions.feedback: Achieng has a family. Families come in many shapes.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

outcomes.text: recognise God as the creator of Adam and Eve
describe how Adam and Eve disobeyed God
state four results of Adam’s disobedience
desire to exercise obedience in day-to-day life

skills.name: Recognise God as the creator of Adam and Eve and describe how they disobeyed God (Genesis 2-3)
skills.mastery: Says God formed Adam from the dust of the ground and breathed life into him (Genesis 2:7), made Eve from Adam's rib (Genesis 2:21-22), told them not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 2:16-17), and that the serpent tempted Eve, she ate and gave to Adam, and he ate (Genesis 3:6). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: God as the creator of the sky, sun, moon and stars comes before the creation of people. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Obeying God's commands, met in the call of Samuel. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: State four results of Adam's disobedience (Genesis 3:16-23)
skills.mastery: States results of the disobedience: they knew they were naked and hid from God, the ground was cursed so man would work hard (sweat) for food (Genesis 3:17-19), pain for the woman in childbirth (3:16), people would return to dust (die) (3:19), and they were sent out of the Garden of Eden (3:23). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: The story of the disobedience comes before its results. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Reasons for obeying, from Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Says the Bible names the fruit as an apple.

example.question: What does Genesis say about the fruit Adam and Eve ate?
example.correct_answer: It was the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil

misconceptions.cause: Pictures and cartoons show an apple.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It was an apple" beside "It was the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 2:17 and 3:6. The tree is named, not the kind of fruit.
misconceptions.feedback: The Bible calls it the fruit of the tree of knowledge of good and evil. It does not say apple.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Adam ate first and gave the fruit to Eve.

example.question: Who ate the fruit first?
example.correct_answer: Eve, then she gave some to Adam

misconceptions.cause: Adam is named first in the story, so the child thinks he acted first.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Adam" beside "Eve, then she gave some to Adam" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Act out Genesis 3:6 in order with two children.
misconceptions.feedback: Eve ate first and then gave some to Adam.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Eve was made from dust like Adam.

example.question: What did God use to make Eve?
example.correct_answer: A rib from Adam

misconceptions.cause: The child knows one way God made people.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Dust" beside "A rib from Adam" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 2:21-22 with a picture.
misconceptions.feedback: God made Eve from a rib taken from Adam.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks God allowed them to eat from every tree.

example.question: Which tree did God tell Adam not to eat from?
example.wrong_answer: None, they could eat from all
example.correct_answer: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil

misconceptions.cause: The garden was full of good trees, so the rule is forgotten.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "None, they could eat from all" beside "The tree of the knowledge of good and evil" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 2:16-17: every tree except one.
misconceptions.feedback: God said they could eat from every tree except the tree of knowledge of good and evil.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks nothing happened because God forgave them at once.

example.question: What happened to Adam and Eve after they disobeyed?
example.correct_answer: They were sent out of the Garden of Eden

misconceptions.cause: Children are taught God forgives, so punishment is forgotten.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Nothing, God forgave them" beside "They were sent out of the Garden of Eden" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:23. God still cared (he made them clothes), but there were results.
misconceptions.feedback: Disobedience had results: they were sent out of the garden. God still cared for them.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the ground was blessed, not cursed, so food came easily.

example.question: After the disobedience, how would man get food?
example.correct_answer: By hard work and sweat, because the ground was cursed

misconceptions.cause: The child mixes up the words blessed and cursed.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Easily, the ground was blessed" beside "By hard work and sweat, because the ground was cursed" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Genesis 3:17-19 and act out hard digging.
misconceptions.feedback: After they disobeyed, man had to work hard to get food.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Adam and Eve hid from God because they were playing.

example.question: Why did Adam and Eve hide from God?
example.wrong_answer: They were playing hide and seek
example.correct_answer: They were afraid and ashamed because they had disobeyed

misconceptions.cause: Hiding is a game for children.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "They were playing hide and seek" beside "They were afraid and ashamed because they had disobeyed" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Ask how a child feels after breaking a rule. Link with Genesis 3:8-10.
misconceptions.feedback: They hid because they were afraid and ashamed after disobeying.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks Adam and Eve stayed in the garden and only lost one tree.

example.question: Where did Adam and Eve live after they disobeyed?
example.wrong_answer: Still in the Garden of Eden
example.correct_answer: Outside the garden

misconceptions.cause: The story ends for the child at eating the fruit.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Still in the Garden of Eden" beside "Outside the garden" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw the garden with a gate and Adam and Eve outside (Genesis 3:23-24).
misconceptions.feedback: God sent Adam and Eve out of the Garden of Eden.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

outcomes.text: differentiate the Bible from other books as guided in 2 Timothy 3:16A
state the number of books in the New Testament
name the four Gospel books in the New Testament
appreciate the Bible as a guide in their daily life

skills.name: Differentiate the Bible from other books (2 Timothy 3:16)
skills.mastery: Says the Bible is different from other books because all Scripture is God-breathed (inspired by God) and useful for teaching and correcting (2 Timothy 3:16), it is God's word that guides Christians, and it is handled and read with respect; other books are written by people for learning or stories. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

prerequisites.reason: The Bible's Old Testament, from Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
Reading the Bible as the word of God. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: State the number of books in the New Testament and name the four Gospels
skills.mastery: States that the New Testament has 27 books (and the Old Testament 39, 66 in all) and names the four Gospels in order: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John; knows they tell of the life of Jesus. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: how many books in the New Testament

prerequisites.reason: The number of books in the Old Testament. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.
The first two books of the Old Testament. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Bible is just a storybook like other storybooks.

example.question: How is the Bible different from a storybook?
example.correct_answer: It is God's word, inspired by God (2 Timothy 3:16)

misconceptions.cause: The Bible has stories and pictures like storybooks.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is not different" beside "It is God's word, inspired by God (2 Timothy 3:16)" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 2 Timothy 3:16. Compare who gave each book its message.
misconceptions.feedback: The Bible is God's word. It is inspired by God, not like other books.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Bible is different only because it is big or has thin pages.

example.question: What makes the Bible special?
example.correct_answer: It is God's word that guides us

misconceptions.cause: Its size and look are what the child notices.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "It is big and thick" beside "It is God's word that guides us" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Show a small pocket Bible. Still God's word. Size does not make it special.
misconceptions.feedback: The Bible is special because it is God's word, not because of its size.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the pastor or one person wrote the whole Bible.

example.question: Who inspired the writing of the Bible?
example.correct_answer: God, through many writers

misconceptions.cause: The child hears the Bible read by the pastor.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "The pastor" beside "God, through many writers" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Say: many people wrote over many years, and God inspired them (2 Timothy 3:16).
misconceptions.feedback: God inspired many people to write the Bible.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Bible is useful only in church, not in daily life.

example.question: When can the Bible guide us?
example.correct_answer: Every day, at home and at school

misconceptions.cause: The Bible is seen mainly at church.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Only in church" beside "Every day, at home and at school" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read 2 Timothy 3:16 (useful for teaching) and Psalm 119:105 (a lamp to my feet).
misconceptions.feedback: The Bible guides us every day, not only in church.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Gives 39 as the number of New Testament books.

example.question: How many books are in the New Testament?

misconceptions.cause: The child learnt 39 for the Old Testament in Grade 2.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "39" beside "27" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Write OT 39, NT 27, total 66 on a two-part bookshelf.
misconceptions.feedback: The New Testament has 27 books. The Old Testament has 39.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names Acts or Genesis as one of the four Gospels.

example.question: Which of these is a Gospel: Acts or Mark?
example.correct_answer: Mark

misconceptions.cause: Acts comes right after the Gospels and Genesis is a well-known book.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Acts" beside "Mark" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Sing the Gospels in order: Matthew, Mark, Luke, John; then Acts comes next, a different kind of book.
misconceptions.feedback: The four Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names the Gospels in the wrong order (John first).

example.question: Which Gospel comes first in the New Testament?
example.correct_answer: Matthew

misconceptions.cause: John is a familiar name and is said first.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "John" beside "Matthew" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Use the first letters M, M, L, J in a chant and on flashcards.
misconceptions.feedback: The Gospels go Matthew, Mark, Luke, John.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Gospels are in the Old Testament.

example.question: In which part of the Bible are the four Gospels?
example.correct_answer: The New Testament

skills.name: Retell the coming of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost and identify his work in a Christian's life (Acts 2:1-4)
skills.mastery: Retells Acts 2:1-4: on the day of Pentecost the disciples were together in one place; a sound like a violent wind came from heaven; what looked like tongues of fire rested on each of them; they were filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke in other languages. Identifies the work of the Holy Spirit: he helps, comforts, guides, teaches, gives strength and helps Christians pray. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: a work of the Holy Spirit
what the disciples saw and heard

prerequisites.reason: The promise Jesus gave his disciples, from Grade 2. Proposed, to confirm by a CRE teacher.

skills.name: Identify five fruit of the Holy Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23)
skills.mastery: Names at least five of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control), knows they are ways of behaving, not fruits we eat, and spots them in everyday actions (sharing is kindness, waiting your turn is patience). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
question_forms: is this a fruit of the Spirit
which fruit is shown in this story

misconceptions.error: Thinks the disciples' heads were burnt by real fire.

example.question: What rested on the disciples at Pentecost?
example.correct_answer: What looked like tongues of fire, without burning them

misconceptions.cause: Fire always burns in the child's experience.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Real fire that burnt them" beside "What looked like tongues of fire, without burning them" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Acts 2:3: what seemed to be tongues of fire.
misconceptions.feedback: Something like tongues of fire rested on them. It did not burn them.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks a real storm blew the house down.

example.question: What did the disciples hear at Pentecost?
example.wrong_answer: A storm that blew the house down
example.correct_answer: A sound like a violent wind from heaven

misconceptions.cause: Wind is linked with storms and damage.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "A storm that blew the house down" beside "A sound like a violent wind from heaven" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Acts 2:2: a sound like wind, filling the house.
misconceptions.feedback: They heard a sound like a strong wind from heaven.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Mixes Pentecost with Christmas or Easter.

example.question: What happened on the day of Pentecost?
example.correct_answer: The Holy Spirit came on the disciples

misconceptions.cause: All church festivals feel alike.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Jesus was born" beside "The Holy Spirit came on the disciples" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Make a three-card line: Christmas (birth), Easter (rose), Pentecost (Holy Spirit came).
misconceptions.feedback: At Pentecost the Holy Spirit came on the disciples.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the Holy Spirit's work is to give magic powers or riches.

example.question: Name a work of the Holy Spirit in a Christian's life.
example.correct_answer: He guides, comforts and helps Christians

misconceptions.cause: Power is pictured as magic in stories.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "He makes people rich" beside "He guides, comforts and helps Christians" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: List the roles from John 14:26 and Luke 24:49 in simple words: helper, teacher, comforter, strength.
misconceptions.feedback: The Holy Spirit guides, comforts and helps Christians.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher of the school's own tradition (FAITH: the wording touches belief or practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks the fruit of the Spirit are real fruits like mangoes.

example.question: Is a mango a fruit of the Holy Spirit?
example.correct_answer: No, the fruit of the Spirit are ways of behaving like love and joy

misconceptions.cause: The word fruit means food to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Yes" beside "No, the fruit of the Spirit are ways of behaving like love and joy" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Draw a tree with words on it: love, joy, peace. Say: these grow in our lives.
misconceptions.feedback: The fruit of the Spirit are good ways of living, like love and kindness.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Names money or cleverness as a fruit of the Spirit.

example.question: Which is a fruit of the Spirit: patience or money?
example.correct_answer: Patience

misconceptions.cause: Good things in life feel like gifts from God.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Money" beside "Patience" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Read Galatians 5:22-23 and circle each fruit.
misconceptions.feedback: Patience is a fruit of the Spirit. Money is not.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Cannot match an action to its fruit, calling waiting your turn "joy".

example.question: Juma waits calmly for his turn on the swing. Which fruit is this?
example.correct_answer: Patience

misconceptions.cause: All good behaviour feels the same to the child.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "Joy" beside "Patience" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Act out each fruit and guess its name.
misconceptions.feedback: Waiting calmly for your turn shows patience.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

misconceptions.error: Thinks there is only one fruit of the Spirit, love.

example.question: How many fruit of the Spirit are named in Galatians 5:22-23?
example.correct_answer: Nine

misconceptions.cause: Love is mentioned most in church.
misconceptions.reveals: Offer "One, love" beside "Nine" and ask the child to choose.
misconceptions.help: Count the nine fruit on the board.
misconceptions.feedback: Galatians 5:22-23 names nine fruit of the Spirit.
misconceptions.source: To confirm by a CRE teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.
